_what: What outside the screen can follow the sound, and what can say what is playing: each row is one service, read through the person's own connection with a Workshop web row marked runs_quietly (records/workshop-ambience-tool-records.json), so nothing is kept for each send. `lights`: where a service's lights come from (`list`: a quiet row to ask, `items` the path to the list in its answer, `id` and `label` paths in each item, `keep` the item facts a send needs; or `fixed`: targets that need no listing), how often each may be sent to (`every_ms`, kept under the service's own limit), and the quiet row that sets one (`set`, its input built from `{ "paint": <fact> }` (colour as #rrggbb, rgb, lit_rgb: the colour dimmed by the brightness, brightness 0..1, percent 1..100, seconds), `{ "item": <fact kept from the list> }` and `{ "join": [ ... ] }`). `playing`: a quiet row that says what is playing, and the paths to its title, who made it and its picture. `music`: the places music plays, offered as pictures on the Ambience screen; a press listens to the computer's sound so the look moves with whatever plays there (`page`: where it plays on the web, `picture`: its mark). Each `lights` row also carries the plain words for what it is (`plain`, `about`), shown wherever the person picks lights. A new light or music service is one row here and its tool rows; nothing in code names a service.
